items.race_condition: The whole field starts together on the widest avenue and nobody may be paced
The leader is released first and every metre of the gap must be closed on feel
Three legs handed over at the mirror pylons, and a dropped handover restarts the leg
Four repetitions down the same straight, each one shorter and required to be quicker
One runner on the road at a time, no field to read and no pace to sit behind
The continent champion enters the field and takes the inside line at the bell
Start positions are set by last month verified volume, so the fittest chases
The clock runs on loam that takes a fraction back from every stride
Legs are handed over at the springs, and the crew total is the only result
The quarry picks the softest line and the chaser has to accept it or lose ground
Five repetitions with the recovery shortening rather than the repetition
The champion starts on the firm inside boardwalk and everyone else on loam
Repetitions run outward from the cool mouth toward the hottest gallery
The champion is handed the shaded line and the field runs the radiant side
The gun goes at the coolest hour and the heat arrives with the second half
Departure slots are ten minutes apart, so no two runners meet the same heat
The head start is measured in degrees, not seconds: hotter starters leave first
The chaser sets off once the leader reaches the vent, with the worst of it ahead
Handovers land at the turns, so one crew member always draws the headwind legs
Starting order is drawn so the slowest runner gets the tailwind opening
Out into the wind and back with it, four times, and only the outbound half counts
A single loop that meets the wind from all four sides in turn
Shelter at the front of the pack is finite and openly contested
The champion is required to lead every headwind section unshielded
Head starts are sized so the whole field arrives at the span together
The span is empty, so the surge is against nobody and has to be self-imposed
Every leg change happens on the pier, and the span is always someone second half
The champion enters the span first by right and the width does the rest
The gap has to be closed before the span or it cannot be closed at all
Eight runners, one span, and the order onto it is decided in the surge
Head starts are paid back in corners rather than seconds
The quarry disappears round every bend, so the gap is run on memory
Each repetition adds one more corner to the same total distance
Eight abreast into a corner wide enough for three, and no contact allowed
The clock rewards the tightest line, which is also the roughest surface
The champion holds the inside for the first lap and must give it up for the last
The runner ahead may be a reflection, and chasing the wrong one costs the race
No distance markers exist, so the plan has to be written before the start
Nobody is told the size of the head start they were given
Handover points are found by counting strides, not by seeing them
Repetitions are called by time while the distance stays unknown
The champion knows the true line across the basin and does not share it
The champion is allowed a warm-up and the rest of the field is not
Everyone goes off cold together and the first kilometre is a trap for all eight
The opening split is thrown away and only what follows is timed
Head starts are given to whoever warms up slowest, measured beforehand
Every leg starts cold, so each handover repeats the same opening problem
The chaser starts warm and the leader started cold, and both know it
Each repetition is required to be quicker than the one before or the set is void
Every leg is scored on its own second half, not on the crew total
The halfway split is published live and the second half is graded against it
The head start is refunded to whoever runs the truest negative split
The leader is released slowly and only a faster finish ever closes it
The champion states her halfway target aloud and the field may match it
Alone in the dense air, with nobody to share the front of it
Head starts are set so the field converges into one pack by halfway
A lone leader against a pack that is cheaper to run in than to escape
Two runners share every leg and both times are recorded
Eight in one gallery, and whoever leads longest finishes worst
The champion is barred from the pack and must run the whole way clear of it
Belt speeds are set individually and never adjusted once the race begins
The champion belt is set to her exact season average and left there
The belt steps up one notch per repetition and never steps back down
Two belts, one gap, and the only variable left is who can hold on
A published target pace, a belt that holds it, and no excuses available
Eight belts at one identical speed until the first runner steps off
All eleven continent champions are in the field at once and none of them is pacing
Eleven laps, each borrowing a different continent road, one attempt at the set
Head starts are computed from every continent result the runner has recorded
The gap is set on the wind lap and has to be closed on the heat lap
Each leg is a different borrowed road and no crew member may repeat one
Eleven repetitions, one per worldline, and the last is the shortest and hardest
